data.title: Acrokeratosis verruciformis of Hopf — viva
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Acrokeratosis verruciformis of Hopf** (Genodermatoses)_

**Q1. What is acrokeratosis verruciformis of Hopf (AKV)?**
- Rare autosomal dominant genodermatosis (ATP2A2 — SERCA2 calcium pump, allelic with Darier's disease) presenting in childhood with multiple flat-topped, skin-coloured, wart-like papules on the dorsa of hands and feet, knees, elbows; may coexist with Darier's disease

**Q2. Clinical features.**
- Small (1–5 mm) polygonal flat warty papules, punctate keratoses and pits on palms/soles, nail changes (thickening, longitudinal ridging, leukonychia); asymptomatic; persists lifelong

**Q3. Histopathology.**
- Hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, acanthosis and papillomatosis with circumscribed elevations resembling 'church spires'; no acantholysis or dyskeratosis (vs Darier's) and no koilocytes (vs warts)

**Q4. Define and classify genodermatoses (PYQ).**
- Genodermatoses: inherited single-gene (or chromosomal) disorders with skin manifestations
- By inheritance: autosomal dominant (NF1, TSC, Darier's, Hailey–Hailey, AKV), autosomal recessive (XP, lamellar ichthyosis, Netherton, PXE), X-linked recessive (X-linked ichthyosis, Fabry, Menkes, Wiskott–Aldrich), X-linked dominant (incontinentia pigmenti, Goltz, CHILD, Conradi–Hünermann), mitochondrial, mosaic
- By system/pathway: disorders of keratinisation, blistering (EB), pigmentation, DNA repair (XP, Bloom, Cockayne, Rothmund–Thomson, trichothiodystrophy), connective tissue (PXE, Ehlers–Danlos, Marfan, cutis laxa), vascular, ectodermal dysplasias, tumour syndromes, neurocutaneous (phakomatoses), metabolic (porphyrias)

**Q5. Differential diagnosis.**
- Plane warts (koilocytes, Koebner), seborrhoeic keratoses (stucco keratosis in elderly), Darier's disease (acral papules + seborrhoeic distribution), epidermodysplasia verruciformis, lichen planus, acrokeratoelastoidosis (marginal papules)

**Q6. Management.**
- Benign; cryotherapy, shave/curettage, CO2/Er:YAG laser, topical retinoids/keratolytics; oral acitretin for extensive lesions; genetic counselling

**Q7. Differential diagnosis in detail.**
- Plane warts (Koebner, HPV, resolve), epidermodysplasia verruciformis, stucco keratoses (elderly), seborrhoeic keratoses, Darier's disease acral lesions (look for seborrhoeic papules elsewhere), lichen planus, acrokeratoelastoidosis (keratotic papules at palm margins)

**Q8. Management in detail.**
- Usually cosmetic; superficial ablation — cryotherapy, CO2/ Er:YAG laser, curettage, electrodesiccation; topical retinoids/ keratolytics; oral acitretin for extensive disease; recurrence possible

**Q9. What is acrokeratoelastoidosis?**
- Autosomal dominant (or sporadic) small firm translucent/ keratotic papules along the margins of palms and soles (at junction of dorsal and ventral skin); histology — fragmented elastic fibres (elastorrhexis) with hyperkeratosis

**Q10. Why is skin biopsy important in AKV?**
- To differentiate from plane warts (koilocytes, HPV) and from acral lesions of Darier's disease (acantholysis and dyskeratosis); AKV shows only church-spire hyperkeratosis without dyskeratosis — diagnosis affects genetic counselling

**Q11. What does 'genodermatosis with ATP2A2' teach about calcium in the skin?**
- Calcium gradient (low basal, high granular) controls keratinocyte differentiation and desmosome assembly; SERCA2 (Darier/ AKV) and SPCA1 (Hailey–Hailey) pump defects disrupt intracellular calcium stores → acantholysis/ dyskeratosis

**Q12. Onset and course.**
- Appears in early childhood or adolescence, slowly progressive, persists lifelong; asymptomatic

**Q13. What is the genetic basis and relation to Darier's disease?**
- Autosomal dominant ATP2A2 (SERCA2) mutations — same gene as Darier's disease; AKV-like lesions occur in ~30–70% of Darier's patients; isolated AKV is considered an allelic variant

**Q14. What is the histopathological pattern?**
- Hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, acanthosis and papillomatosis with circumscribed epidermal elevations resembling 'church spires'; no dyskeratosis or acantholysis (unlike Darier's)

**Q15. Associated nail and palmar findings.**
- Nail changes (thick, white, longitudinal ridging, subungual hyperkeratosis), punctate keratoses/pits on palms; lesions are flat-topped skin-coloured warty papules on dorsa of hands/feet, knees, elbows

## Quick spotter facts
- Flat wart-like papules on dorsa of hands since childhood, 'church-spire' histology — AKV of Hopf (ATP2A2)

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Genodermatoses — ATP2A2 spectrum). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
